library(reticulate)

## The question

How well do the computer-vision models on the WildObs Image Management Platform
(WIMP) perform on real camera-trap images? A WIMP AI result has two stages:
MegaDetector decides whether an image holds an animal, a person, a vehicle or
nothing, and a regional species classifier names the animal. Errors at either
stage reach users, so the benchmark scores both.

## The method

Colin Broughton's benchmark workflow (WildObs, 2026) scores a model by running
images whose true label is known through the WIMP and comparing the AI output with
the truth. Each test class gets its own deployment, tagged with the true label, in
a project configured with the model under test. This repository automates every
step around Colin's evaluation so that any WildObs user can run it from four inputs.

| Step | File | What happens | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `01_inputs.Rmd` | The four inputs | user |
| 2 | `02_select_images.Rmd` | Pick validated images from existing WIMP projects | API, read-only |
| 3 | `03_wimp_projects.Rmd` | One benchmark project per model run | WIMP web UI |
| 4 | `04_upload_and_ai.Rmd` | Deployments, upload, AI | API |
| 5 | `05_export.Rmd` | Camtrap DP tables per run | API |
| 6 | `06_evaluate.Rmd` | Colin's reports + detector metrics | local |
| 7 | `07_dashboard.Rmd` | Comparison across runs | local |

## Running a step

Every step is one command. In R Markdown the chunks call the same Python module.

```{python eval=FALSE}
import subprocess
subprocess.run(["python", "-m", "wimpbench", "check", "--config", "config/awt_2026_11.yaml"], check=True)
```

These files convert to Jupyter notebooks one-to-one (each `python` chunk becomes a
code cell, the text a markdown cell), e.g. with `jupytext --to ipynb docs/*.Rmd`.
